transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Your dishwasher is letting water escape, but we can't say why until we know where it's coming from, as leaks can start at the door, a hose or inside the machine. With water on the floor and sockets right next to it, don't touch the plug or sockets while anything is wet; if you need to cut the power, use the switch at your consumer unit (fuse box). From what you have described, the most likely cause is is there water in the base, and where is it leaking from (find the source first). Next: Establish whether there is water in the base tray and where it is coming from. Let me know what you find.
its coming from the bottom of the door, loads of suds and water, still running now. water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor and the socket is on the wall next to it. im scared

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal / gasket. Open the door and look all the way round the rubber seal on the tub edge, and along the bottom of the door, for splits, flattened sections or something caught on it. Is the seal damaged, was something caught on it (now removed), or does it look fine?
the seal looks ok i think, not split or anything. its still running tho, should i turn it off?? my housemate put fairy washing up liquid in cos we ran out of tablets

Yes, turn it off now, but because water is spreading toward the extension lead and wall socket, don't touch any plug, socket or lead while you're standing in water or they're wet. Next: Clean/inspect the door seal and check the door sits square. Let me know what you find.
ok i turned it off. theres still loads of suds inside and the water is nearly at the extension lead. what do i do now??

Tall trays or items hanging below the lower rack can deflect the spray straight at the door seal. With the racks loaded, turn each spray arm by hand. Was anything catching the arms or pointing at the door (and have you moved it), or is everything clear?
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
its turned off now so the arms arent moving?? i dont know about that, the water is nearly at the extension lead, can i unplug it or what do i do
Next: Check the lower spray arm isn't split. Let me know what you find.
